text:
marta: Heads-up — I ran a focused profiling sweep on KV compression with INT8 vs FP8 for our 32k-context LlamaX runs. Quick summary: INT8 gives the best memory reduction but we've got a measurable decode-quality drift on long prefixes. Posting numbers and the repro command below.

devon: dropping in — nice, can you paste the p95/p99 numbers? also which kernel was used for INT8 decode?

marta: p50/p95/p99 for decode latency (single token, warm cache, batch=1):
- baseline FP32-KV: 1.8ms / 4.6ms / 9.2ms
- FP8-KV (e4m2-ish): 1.5ms / 3.9ms / 8.4ms
- INT8-KV (symmetric per-row): 1.3ms / 3.3ms / 7.6ms
Memory (KV size for 32k ctx, 4096 head-dim model):
- FP32: 4.0 GB
- FP8: 2.0 GB
- INT8: 1.0 GB
Quality (long prefix generation A/B on our eval set):
- FP8 vs FP32: small BLEU/ROUGE/perp delta (~0.8% loss on some prompts)
- INT8 vs FP32: larger drift (~3.6% on the same prompts), specific failure modes: repeated token loops on >8k prefixes, mild semantic collapse for some multi-step QA chains

jlee: interesting. which kernel path did the runtime pick for INT8? did it fall back to slower GEMM for any shapes?

marta: runtime selected the new int8-packed KV kernel (kv_int8_pack_v2) for most shapes. We saw fallback to generic attention for edge-case sequence lengths (like when sequence length % 64 != 0) — those fallbacks explain the small p99 tails.

infra-bot: deploy-note: canary of kv_int8_pack_v2 rolled to dedicated-gpu-3 at 2026-02-12T08:12Z

devon: calibration details? we need to know if the INT8 quant used a global scale or per-row per-head. that impacts drift a lot.

marta: INT8 used per-row min/max + symmetric quant, with simple percentile clipping at 99.9th. FP8 used dynamic shared exponent (e4m2) with per-head scaling extracted during the calibration pass. The INT8 path was calibrated with a 512-token sample set, FP8 with same sample set but different scaling logic.

jlee: can you try per-head quant scales for INT8? last time per-head reduced semantic drift on QA chains. also try raising clipping to 99.995 to preserve tails.

marta: yea plan to run a follow-up. early signs: per-head drops the decode regressions by about 40% but adds ~5% more memory overhead (since we store extra scale vectors). I'll schedule a comparison.

devon: batching heuristics — were you testing continuous batching / KV cache reuse? or isolated single-token throughput?

marta: both. The numbers above are single-token with warm KV cache. For continuous-batched streaming (batch=8, interleaved prefixes) INT8 still wins cost-wise, but we saw increased variance when batching mixed sequence lengths due to cache alignment + kernel tiling inefficiencies. Profiling trace shows extra reorders on the INT8 packed format when batch shapes are heterogeneous.

jlee: that's consistent — the int8 kernel assumes aligned strides for packed rows. for mixed-len batches we should trigger a fallback to an unpack-and-run path that avoids reorders. Could be worth implementing a small heuristics check in the scheduler: if >30% of batch shapes mismatch, use unpack path.

marta: noted. I'll add a micro-benchmark to quantify the overhead of unpack path vs fallback GEMM.

devon: what about downstream quality monitoring? can we surface per-request quality deltas so we can auto-fall back to FP32/FP8 for risky prompts?

marta: we currently log a per-route perplexity estimate and a small set of diagnostic tokens. Idea: keep a short rolling eval on live traffic for candidates (e.g., long-context QA routes). If anomaly score > threshold, route to FP8/FP32. This is doable in the console as a rollout policy.

sre_oncall: if we add auto-fallback in routing, make sure to add circuit-breaker counters — we don't want a hot route to cascade fallback and exceed capacity. Also tie the fallback to dedicated capacity tiers.

marta: good call. We'll gate auto-fallback to customers on Dedicated or higher tiers by default.

devon: one more ask — can you attach the exact profiling command and the perftrace snippet that highlighted the reorder penalty?

marta: paste of the command I used:
```
./tools/kv_profiler --model-path /models/llamax-4b --ctx 32768 --quant int8 --calib-samples 512 --batch-shapes "1,1;8,1024;8,4096" --trace perftrace.json
```
perftrace snippet (abridged):
- step 1023: kv_int8_pack_v2: pack_reorder 1.8ms, pack_copy 0.9ms; exec 1.2ms
- step 2048: fallback_unpacked_gemm: unpack 2.7ms, gemm 1.4ms
- step 3072: kv_fp8_pack: pack_reorder 0.5ms; exec 1.3ms

jlee: that packing cost on INT8 is concerning. If unpack path is cheaper than repeated reorder, it may pay off to detect and use it. Also consider adding a small LRU knob for pack buffers keyed by shape to avoid re-packing for common shapes.

marta: added to action items.

devon: can you run a short quality regression check with the per-head INT8 and FP8 and post the fail-prompt examples? we need repros for SRE and model team.

marta: will do. ETA EOD. I'll create a canary job that runs: 1) FP32 baseline, 2) FP8, 3) INT8 (global), 4) INT8 (per-head). I'll attach diffs and sample failures.

sre_oncall: also record the hardware topology in the trace (SM usage, memory clock) — some of these pack/reorder costs correlate with PCI bandwidth on multi-gpu boxes.

marta: ack. adding sm_usage and memcpy stats to the trace.

infra-bot: ticket created: RH-6642 "kv quant: int8 per-head perf/quality follow-up" assigned to marta, devon, jlee

devon: solid. thanks for the thorough profiling. let's meet tomorrow 10am to decide rollout policy and a quick scheduler patch for unpack heuristics. :calendar: 

marta: thanks all. will upload the perftrace.json and sample diffs in the thread when ready. :thumbsup:
